title: Environmental Economics
tagline: Pollution and policy instruments, valuing the environment, cost–benefit analysis and discounting, non-renewable and renewable resources, climate economics, international agreements and green growth
summary: The environment provides resources and absorbs waste, but markets rarely price these services. This course applies economic tools to environmental problems: the choice between standards, taxes and tradable permits; the valuation of environmental goods; cost–benefit analysis and discounting over long horizons; the management of non-renewable and renewable resources such as minerals, fisheries and forests; and the economics of climate change, international environmental agreements and the energy transition.

chapters.title: The environment and the economy
chapters.summary: Pollution as an externality, the materials balance, sustainability and the measurement of green national income.

chapters.title: Instruments of environmental policy
chapters.summary: Standards, Pigouvian taxes and tradable permits, cost-effectiveness, and prices versus quantities under uncertainty.

chapters.title: Valuing the environment
chapters.summary: Use and non-use values, revealed-preference methods such as travel cost and hedonic pricing, and stated-preference methods.

chapters.title: Cost–benefit analysis and discounting
chapters.summary: Appraising projects, the social discount rate, intergenerational equity and decisions under uncertainty.

chapters.title: Non-renewable resources
chapters.summary: Hotelling’s rule, optimal extraction paths, scarcity and the evidence on resource prices.

chapters.title: Renewable resources: fisheries and forests
chapters.summary: Biological growth, open access and the tragedy of the commons, optimal harvesting and forest rotation.

chapters.title: The economics of climate change
chapters.summary: Integrated assessment models, the social cost of carbon, carbon pricing and the choice of mitigation path.

chapters.title: International environmental agreements
chapters.summary: Transboundary pollution, free riding between countries, the stability of agreements and carbon leakage.

chapters.title: Energy, innovation and green growth
chapters.summary: Directed technical change, energy transitions, and the debate over growth and the environment.
